cases.original_forecast: At approximately constant headspace and temperature, the pressure increments from added gases are approximately additive, with small gas-solubility differences.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Compare pressure increments rather than treating the initial headspace as a vacuum.
original_criteria_review.reason: The saved sealed-air baseline is101324.630104Pa; the two positive increments are2478.957599Pa each rather than pressures measured from vacuum.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Use the actual gas-phase moles and temperature in P = nRT/V; O2 and N2 need not dissolve equally.
original_criteria_review.reason: Independent dose-plus-baseline nRT/V calculations use each actual temperature and1L headspace and agree within the existing molar inventory resolution; both exact pressure residuals are retained. This selects ideal finite-carrier additivity, without a quantitative N2/O2 dissolution claim.

material_projection.scope: Whole-bench represented owned atoms and charge plus recorded air, solvent and exports; catalase is a molecular tracer. No per-vessel transfer or energy validation.

cases.scope: Original finite ideal-carrier/aqueous carbonate teaching domain. No quantitative N2/O2 solubility, real-gas/high-pressure, empirical partition calibration, reaction heat or latest-production claim.

cases.original_forecast: The alkaline liquid converts CO2 into bicarbonate/carbonate, storing more carbon in liquid and reducing the CO2 contribution to pressure.

original_criteria_review.criterion: Compare carbon partition fractions at the actual temperatures.
original_criteria_review.reason: Owned aqueous/gas carbon fractions and CO2 partial pressures are independently calculated at both recorded temperatures; the warmer alkaline arm retains more carbon in solution and has lower CO2 partial pressure.

original_criteria_review.criterion: The alkaline vessel retains the added carbon; pressure reduction alone must not be mistaken for carbon deletion.
original_criteria_review.reason: Both finite CO2 additions close against their own trapped-air baseline. Whole-bench atoms/charge also close at the existing1e-8mol/eq audit resolution; decreased pressure is not carbon deletion.
